proposals.expected_failure_mode: H compartment may be weakly identifiable in a short series; H may absorb reporting/ascertainment effects and misattribute timing vs magnitude.
proposals.rationale: Target is weekly hospitalization rate; mapping observations directly to an explicit H compartment aligns with surveillance semantics while keeping dynamics simple (single hospitalization state).

proposals.expected_failure_mode: Conflates infectious prevalence and hospitalization burden; may over-smooth peaks or inflate inferred infectious burden when admissions dominate.
proposals.rationale: If reported hospitalization rate reflects a mixture of severe incident infections and admissions (or coding that partially tracks infectious burden), observing I+H can provide robustness to timing mismatch between infection and admission processes.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: Delay may be season- or age-specific; fixed 2-week lag can misalign peak timing and distort amplitude if true lag varies over time.
proposals.rationale: Parsimonious template consistent with discovered patterns; a 2-week delay captures plausible lag from infection to hospitalization without introducing an explicit H state that may be hard to identify.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: Over-long delay can shift peaks too late and force compensatory parameter behavior (e.g., faster transmission) to match observed timing.
proposals.rationale: Alternative lag choice to cover longer infection-to-admission delays; retains SEIRS parsimony while matching recommended delayed observation semantics.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: If reinfection/waning immunity matters within-season, SEIR may underfit tail behavior and misrepresent post-peak persistence.
proposals.rationale: Simpler than SEIRS when waning immunity is not strongly expressed within the training window; delayed_I addresses hospitalization lag while minimizing compartments.
